newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin may sign 1997 budget on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin may sign 1997 budget on Tuesday.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin may sign the 1997 budget into law on Tuesday, a spokesman for the presidential press service said on Monday.
Yeltsin will receive the document later on Monday, after his staff have finished checking it, he said in answer to an enquiry.

The Federation Council upper house of parliament passed the budget on February 12 after it was approved by the State Duma lower house last month, and it now only awaits Yeltsin's signature to come into force.
The budget sets a deficit of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product according to Russian calculations on revenues of 434 trillion roubles and spending of 529.8 trillion roubles.
The International Monetary Fund wants the budget to be passed so that it can agree a 1997 economic programme with Russia under its current $10 billion three-year loan.
